title: Kinetic Molecular and Atomic Theory
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Kinetic Molecular and Atomic Theory Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: The behaviour of matter can be explained by the kinetic molecular theory and atomic theory: particles in motion, states of matter, protons, neutrons and electrons, and models of the atom. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 8, Chemistry)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 science worksheets (BC): the kinetic molecular theory, states and changes of state, atomic models, and protons, neutrons and electrons. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: All matter is made of particles in constant motion.
key_sub: Atoms have protons, neutrons and electrons.
body_html:
How to think about it

The kinetic molecular theory says all matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving. Heating makes them move faster and spread apart, which explains melting, boiling and expansion.

Atoms have a tiny nucleus of protons (positive) and neutrons (no charge), with electrons (negative) around it. The number of protons is the atomic number and decides the element. Models of the atom changed as scientists such as Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford and Bohr found new evidence.

Example

An atom has 6 protons. Which element is it?

Look up atomic number 6.

Answer: carbon

Example

Why does a balloon get bigger in the sun?

The air inside warms up.

Answer: the gas particles move faster and spread out

Common mistakes

  • Thinking particles get bigger when heated (they move faster).
  • Thinking the electrons are in the nucleus.
  • Mixing up atomic number and mass number.

faq.q: Why does a gas fill its container?
faq.a: Its particles move freely in all directions.

faq.q: Are there smaller particles than protons?
faq.a: Yes, protons and neutrons are made of quarks.

items.q: A metal lid on a glass jar is held under hot water and then opens easily. Which explains this?
c: The mass of the substance increases when heated.
The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
The metal lid expands more than the glass when heated.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: How are the particles arranged in a liquid?
c: They are all touching in a gas.
Closely packed in a fixed, orderly arrangement.
Close together but not in fixed positions.
items.e: In a liquid, particles are close together but not in fixed positions and slide past one another.

items.q: How do the particles in a gas move?
c: They do not move at all.
Move quickly and randomly in all directions.
items.e: In a gas, particles are far apart and randomly arranged and move quickly and randomly in all directions.

items.q: A balloon left in the sun gets bigger. Which explains this?
c: The particles themselves become bigger when heated.
The mass of the substance increases when heated.
The air inside expands as its particles move faster and further apart.
items.e: Particles move faster and further apart when heated; they do not grow and no new particles form.

items.q: A drop of ink is added to a beaker of still water. After an hour the water is evenly coloured. What is the best explanation?
c: The water or air particles stopped moving.
The particles were pushed by convection only.
Diffusion: ink particles moved from a higher to a lower concentration.
The particles grew bigger and filled the space.
items.e: Particles are always moving randomly, so there is a net movement from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated.

items.q: What did Niels Bohr contribute?

He described atoms as tiny solid spheres that cannot be divided.
items.e: Models change with evidence.

items.q: An atom has 10 neutrons and 9 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: Use the protons (9), not the neutrons.

items.q: An atom of carbon (C) has a proton number of 6 and a nucleon number of 12. How many electrons does it have?
items.e: An atom is neutral, so it has the same number of electrons as protons.

items.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of aluminum-29?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 29 − 13 = 16.

items.q: An atom has 37 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: The number of protons decides the element.

items.q: An atom has 21 neutrons and 18 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: Use the protons (18), not the neutrons.

items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 80 − 34 = 46.

items.q: An atom has 2 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: Every atom of helium has 2 protons; the proton number identifies the element.

items.q: An atom of neon (Ne) has a proton number of 10 and a nucleon number of 20. How many neutrons does it have?

items.q: A neutral atom of aluminum has a mass number of 27. How many electrons does it have?

items.q: An atom has 7 neutrons and 8 protons. Which element is it?

items.q: How many valence electrons does helium (He) have? (It is in group 18.)
items.e: Groups 1–2: same as the group number. Groups 13–18: subtract 10 (helium has 2).
